title: Non-blocking follow-ups from frontend-position-risk-columns-followups-followups-followups review (PR #260)
description: Non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's review of PR #260 (frontend-position-risk-columns-followups-followups-followups), recorded here so they aren't lost once the PR merges. PR #260 itself was accepted (tests/coverage/lint/type-check all clean, the new StockCharts.test.tsx regression test independently verified to fail on pre-fix code, browser walkthrough of both fixes confirmed in a real Chromium session, e2e suite green).

checklist.step: Compound-failure gap introduced by this PR on StockCharts: PriceChart's own `indicatorsQuery.isError` ErrorState (the one OscillatorChart/VolumeIndicatorsChart/TrendStrengthChart now rely on as their shared failure's sole surface) is gated behind `showOverlaySection = historyQuery.isSuccess && hasBars && overlayEnabled` (PriceChart.tsx), not just `indicatorsQuery.isError` alone -- a pre-existing gate unrelated to error ownership. If `GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/history` itself fails, or succeeds with zero usable bars (e.g. every returned bar filtered out by `hasFiniteOhlc`, such as a very thin/new ticker with only a still-forming latest bar), `showOverlaySection` is false, so PriceChart's own indicators-ErrorState never renders -- even if `GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/indicators` genuinely failed at the same time (e.g. a 422 for insufficient weekly history). Before this PR, each of the three now-suppressed charts rendered its own independent, ungated ErrorState in that scenario, so a real indicators failure was still visible somewhere; after this PR, in that specific compound-failure case, nothing surfaces the indicators failure at all (the user only sees PriceChart's own 'No price history available' EmptyState/its own historyQuery ErrorState, with three silently blank chart sections below it). Independently confirmed by pr-reviewer's own read of PriceChart.tsx and corroborated by a parallel code-review pass. Worth deciding whether PriceChart's indicators-ErrorState should be un-gated from `showOverlaySection` for this specific error path, or whether one of the three siblings should fall back to showing its own ErrorState when `!showOverlaySection` is also true.

OscillatorChart/VolumeIndicatorsChart/TrendStrengthChart's suppression of their own `indicatorsQuery.isError` ErrorState is a hard-coded, unconditional assumption baked into each component (not an opt-in prop) that PriceChart is always mounted as a sibling and owns this failure -- the same implicit-render-order/co-occurrence coupling this same PR explicitly identified and fixed via an opt-in `errorSurfacedBySibling` prop for SellFlaggedPositionsCard, but deliberately did not apply here (per this task's own `decisions` entry, which explicitly scoped that robustness question to SellFlaggedPositionsCard only, per the checklist item's own wording instructing replication of existing precedent). Confirmed by grep that only `StockCharts.tsx` currently imports/uses these three components, so the assumption holds today, but nothing structurally prevents a future standalone reuse (a new page, a Storybook story, a narrower composition) from silently losing this specific error's visibility, the exact same failure mode already fixed once this PR for SellFlaggedPositionsCard. Worth applying the same explicit-prop (or equivalent order-independent) treatment here if/when these components are ever reused outside StockCharts.tsx, or documenting the coupling more explicitly in the meantime (e.g. a runtime dev-mode warning, or a lint rule) rather than only a code comment.
